messages.author: 5b9f4c138fd9a813
messages.subject: Plotting
parts:
Hi geomorph community, 

I am currently trying to use plotTangentSpace to perform a PCA to a set of 22 different species. So far I have imported the TPS files (one file for each species) and performed separate gpa analysis, likewise, one for each species. My question is about the plotTangentSpace function, how can I perform a unique PCA for every species that I have?  Will I have to change the TPS files, uniting each one of them, or is there another way to do that? 

Thanks in advance,
--
Diniz Ferreira
Graduando em Ciências Biológicas
Laboratório de Evolução e Genética de Insetos (LEGIN)
DEZG - IB - Universidade Federal de Pelotas

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: Plotting
parts:
I am not entirely clear about your question. If you have something like:

gpa.species1=gpagen(tps.for.species1)
gpa.species2=gpagen(tps.for.species2)
...

you should be able to do

pca.species1=plotTangentCoordinates(gpa.species1$coords)
pca.species2=plotTangentCoordinates(gpa.species2$coords)

and these pca results will be independent of each other...

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: Plotting
parts:
Yes, that definitely clears. But I don't think what you want is possible with individual species gpas because

1. If your species have different set of landmarks, then the dimensionality of covariance matrices will be different, eigenvectors have different lengths.
2. Each PCA will be centered around the species mean gpa is conducted on, so the scores will loose their meaning when you try concatenate results across different analysis.

Is there a reason you cannot combine your all your species in the same GPA? Different number or configuration of landmarks?
